\tabnotes{The dependent variable is the duration-standardised,
  maturity-averaged one-year excess return $\rxbar_{t+12}$ \eqref{eq:rxbar} for
  the United States, 1990m1--2014m12 ($300$ observations). Column~(1) uses the
  yields at the six available maturities; column~(2) adds trend inflation
  $\tau^{\mathrm{CPI}}_{t}$; columns~(3) and~(4) use the one-year yield and the
  average yield $\bar{y}_{t}$, without and with trend inflation; column~(5)
  uses the one-year cycle $\cyc^{(1)}_{t}$ and the average cycle $\cycbar_{t}$.
  $t$-statistics in parentheses are Newey--West adjusted ($18$ lags). Wald is
  the statistic of the joint test that all slope coefficients are zero, with
  its $p$-value below. Rel.\ prob.\ (BIC) is the relative posterior model
  probability $\exp\{(\mathrm{BIC}_{\mathrm{best}}-\mathrm{BIC}_{i})/2\}$,
  equal to one for the best-fitting model (\Cref{sec:meth-inference}). The
  table replicates \citet{cieslak2015}, Table~2, Panel~A.}
